Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the Vitality Brands Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.  

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Vitality Brands' Q3 results. With me on the call are Jamie Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; and Lisa Gomez, Chief Supply Chain Officer; and other members of our leadership team.  

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.  

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jamie Thompson.  

Jamie Thompson:  
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Vitality Brands delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment marked by persistent inflation, shifting consumer preferences toward health and wellness, and heightened competition, yet we remain focused on executing our strategic priorities to drive sustainable, profitable growth.  

Our discussion today will cover our overall financial performance, including robust organic sales growth and margin expansion; standout brand performance and our innovation pipeline; supply chain and operational efficiencies; marketing and promotional activities with strong ROI; sustainability initiatives embedded across our operations; and our outlook for the remainder of the year with reaffirmed guidance.  

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.  

Sarah Chen:  
Thank you, Jamie. As Jamie mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $15.2 billion, representing a 6% organic increase compared to the prior year. Gross margin was 48.2%, driven by input cost deflation, pricing actions, and productivity gains from our Vitality Edge program. Operating income was $2.8 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $1.45. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.  

Now, let's dive deeper into our gross margin performance, which continues to be a key pillar of our profitability story here at Vitality Brands. For the third quarter, our consolidated gross margin expanded to 48.2%, up a robust 210 basis points year-over-year from 46.1%, and 110 basis points sequentially from Q2's 47.1%. This marks our sixth consecutive quarter of gross margin expansion, underscoring the effectiveness of our multi-year Vitality Edge productivity program and our disciplined pricing amid a still-volatile input cost environment.  

Breaking it down by driver, input cost deflation was the standout contributor, delivering approximately 320 basis points of favorability. We've been navigating elevated commodity prices since post-pandemic supply disruptions, but Q3 saw meaningful relief. Dairy costs, critical for our yogurt and nutritionals portfolio similar to Chobani or Danone's offerings, declined 12% quarter-over-quarter due to normalized milk supply chains in North America and Europe. Packaging materials, about 15% of COGS, fell 8% on lower resin prices post the 2022-2023 petrochemical spikes. Even in cocoa—where prices surged over 100% YTD to near $10,000 per metric ton, pressuring peers like Hershey and Mondelez—our forward hedging program at 70% coverage for FY24 locked in savings of roughly 50 basis points.  

Pricing actions added another 180 basis points, reflecting targeted list price increases of 4-6% across most categories, with particular strength in North America where consumer tolerance for premium SKUs remains high. We executed mid-single-digit increases on high-velocity household essentials, like our Tide-like laundry detergents and Bounty-equivalent paper towels, without meaningful volume erosion—elasticity hovered around -0.4, better than the category average of -0.6 per Nielsen data. This pricing power stems from our 45% market share leadership in fabric care and our ongoing premiumization shift, where premium products now represent 28% of sales, up from 22% two years ago.  

Productivity initiatives from Vitality Edge contributed a solid 120 basis points. Our supply chain digitization efforts, including AI-driven demand sensing via partnerships with Blue Yonder—similar to what Unilever and P&G have scaled—reduced inventory obsolescence by 15% and optimized factory yields to 92%, up from 88% last year. We also realized $45 million in savings from zero-based manufacturing redesign, consolidating three plants in APAC into two high-efficiency facilities focused on beverages like our Gatorade-style sports drinks. Sustainable sourcing played a role too: our regenerative agriculture program with palm oil suppliers cut costs by 5% through yield improvements, aligning with EU deforestation regs and appealing to Gen Z consumers.  

Offsetting these tailwinds were a few headwinds. Unfavorable product mix shaved off 90 basis points, driven by disproportionate growth in lower-margin impulse snacks—our Doritos-like portfolio grew 15% on volume, pulling the overall mix down as consumers traded into value packs amid sticky inflation. Foreign exchange was a 40 basis point drag, primarily from a stronger USD impacting our 35% of sales from emerging markets. And freight/logistics, while improved, still pressured by Red Sea disruptions, added a modest 20 basis point offset—though our nearshoring to Mexico for North American distribution mitigated this versus last year.  

Regionally, North America delivered 51.3% gross margins, up 280 bps YoY, fueled by pricing and dairy relief in our powerhouse nutritionals and personal care segments. EMEA held steady at 44.8%, gaining 150 bps despite energy surcharges in Germany and France, where we've offset via localized sourcing for our Hellmann's-style mayos. APAC was the star for growth at 46.1%, up 190 bps, propelled by e-commerce mix in China—platforms like Tmall now 25% of regional sales—and premium beauty launches tailored to K-beauty trends. LatAm lagged at 42.5%, down 50 bps on hyperinflation in Argentina and Brazil currency devaluation, but our hedging and dollar-denominated contracts limited the damage.  

Looking ahead strategically, we're guiding full-year FY24 gross margin to 47.5-48.5%, implying 200-250 bps expansion, ahead of our initial 150 bps target. This embeds continued input cost normalization—we expect mid-single-digit deflation in Q4—and further Vitality Edge savings of $180 million annually. Key initiatives include scaling our precision fermentation tech for plant-based alternatives, targeting 300 bps margin uplift in nutritionals by FY26, much like Impossible Foods' pivot but at consumer scale. We're also investing $200 million in U.S. capacity for high-margin RTD beverages to capture the Prime-like hydration boom, where margins exceed 55%.  

With that foundation, I'll now turn to our key strategic priorities and the meaningful progress we've made in the first half of fiscal 2024. As you know, our "Powering Everyday Essentials" strategy—launched two years ago—remains laser-focused on delivering sustainable, profitable growth in a dynamic CPG landscape. We continue to execute against four interconnected pillars: portfolio optimization for margin expansion, sustainability leadership, digital acceleration, and supply chain resilience with cost discipline.  

First, portfolio optimization for margin expansion. We're relentlessly pruning our portfolio to double down on high-growth, high-margin categories like premium snacks, plant-based beverages, and at-home personal care—segments growing at 8-10% globally per NielsenIQ data, outpacing the broader CPG market's 3-4% trajectory. In Q2, we divested two underperforming legacy brands in North American household cleaners, generating $250 million in proceeds, which we've redeployed into innovation. This contributed to the 120-basis-point improvement in our gross margin to 48.2%, ahead of our 100-basis-point full-year target. Organic sales growth accelerated to 6.2% in Q2, driven by 4% volume/mix and 2.2% pricing—our strongest in three quarters. Market share gains totaled 60 basis points in core categories, per IRI and Circana metrics, with standout performance in plant-based dairy alternatives, where our "GreenLeaf" line captured 12% U.S. share, up from 9% a year ago, chipping away at leaders like Chobani and Oatly. We're on track for 5-7% organic growth for FY24, with premiumization fueling 2 points of that through initiatives like our "Vitality Boost" functional snack platform, which launched 15 SKUs and posted 25% repeat purchase rates in test markets.  

Second, sustainability leadership. Consumers are voting with their wallets—Euromonitor reports 68% of global shoppers now prioritize eco-friendly packaging, up from 52% pre-pandemic. We've embedded ESG into our core operations, targeting net-zero Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2040 and 100% recyclable packaging by 2028. Progress is strong: In H1, 72% of our global packaging portfolio is now recyclable or compostable, up from 55% last year, including our switch to 100% rPET bottles for our flagship "PureSpring" water brand across Europe. Sourcing-wise, 85% of our cocoa and palm oil is RSPO-certified, reducing deforestation risk amid regulatory pressures like the EU Deforestation Regulation. This drove a 15% reduction in Scope 3 emissions year-over-year and unlocked $45 million in green premiums from retailers like Walmart and Tesco. Regionally, in Asia-Pacific—our fastest-growing region at 9% organic growth—our sustainable palm oil initiative with partners like Wilmar has secured 20% cost savings on inputs, buffering 7% cocoa inflation.  

Third, digital acceleration. E-commerce now represents 18% of our global sales, up from 12% two years ago, aligning with the industry's 15-20% penetration trend per McKinsey. We've invested $150 million in our "CPG Nexus" platform—a unified DTC and B2B digital ecosystem powered by AI-driven personalization and Shopify integrations. Q2 e-commerce sales surged 32% YoY, led by North America (25% of total sales) where Amazon and our DTC site drove 40% growth via targeted campaigns on our "FitFuel" protein bars. Technical initiatives include deploying machine learning models for demand sensing, reducing stockouts by 25% and improving forecast accuracy to 92%—on par with best-in-class peers like Reckitt. In China, our Tmall and JD.com partnerships yielded 45% growth, capturing share in the premium beauty segment against L'Oréal and Estée Lauder. Looking ahead, we're piloting AR virtual try-ons for skincare, targeting a 10% uplift in conversion rates by Q4.  

Finally, supply chain resilience with cost discipline. Geopolitical tensions and Red Sea disruptions have spiked ocean freight 30%, but our multi-year "Resilient Core" program—including nearshoring and supplier diversification—delivered $120 million in H1 savings, or 2.2% of COGS. Inventory days on hand stabilized at 65 days, down from 78 peak in 2022, thanks to blockchain traceability pilots with IBM Food Trust for 40% of our produce supply chain. Regionally, Latin America grew 11% organically despite FX headwinds, bolstered by localized production in Brazil for our "TropiFresh" juices. In Europe, where volumes softened 1% amid cost-of-living pressures, pricing discipline and productivity gains lifted EPS contribution by 8%. Overall, adjusted operating margin expanded 90 basis points to 18.5% in Q2.  

In summary, these priorities are delivering: FY24 guidance reaffirmed at 5-7% organic growth, 100-150 basis points of margin expansion, and $1.1-1.2 billion in free cash flow. We're positioned to outperform in a 2-3% CPG market.  

Before I move on, a quick note on geographic performance, which highlights the balance between developed and emerging markets. Total net revenues for the quarter came in at $15.2 billion, up 4% as reported and 6% on an organic basis—excluding the 1% FX headwind and the 1% impact from divestitures like our non-core European confectionery unit. Developed markets—North America, Western Europe, and Australia/New Zealand—accounted for 62% of our sales at $9.4 billion, delivering 2% organic growth. Emerging markets—Latin America, Asia-Pacific ex-Japan, and Middle East/Africa—made up the remaining 38% at $5.8 billion, posting a robust 12% organic growth, even after adjusting for 3 points of unfavorable FX in Brazil and Argentina.  

In developed markets, North America grew 3% organically to $6.1 billion, with our Health & Wellness platforms like "PureLife" beverages seeing 8% volume growth and distribution gains to 92% ACV. Western Europe was flat organically at $2.8 billion, with e-commerce at 18% of sales. Gross margin mix improved to 32.5%, up 80 bps. Emerging markets roared with 12% organic growth: Asia-Pacific up 15%, China yogurts up 22%; Latin America 11%, Brazil beverages up 14%; Middle East/Africa 8%. We're tilting capex to 45% emerging, targeting 45% sales mix by 2025.  

On pricing actions, which have been a cornerstone of our P&L resilience, we executed targeted pricing across our portfolio, achieving net price realization of +6.8% globally, up from +5.2% in Q1. This drove organic net sales growth of 4.2%, with +6.8% from price/mix offset by -2.6% volume—elasticity at -0.4. North America +8.2% NDR, Europe +5.1%, emerging +6.5%. Full-year organic guide +4-5%, pricing +6%.  

I'll now turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss marketing and brand performance.  

Mike Patel:  
Thank you, Sarah. We saw strong performance in our core brands, particularly GreenLeaf. Our digital marketing efforts are driving significant engagement, and we are seeing strong results from our Live Zest campaign.  

Before I hand over, let me expand on our advertising and promotion spend and the strong ROI trajectory. In Q3, we deployed $1.28 billion in A&P, up 4.2% year-over-year on a constant-currency basis, representing 14.1% of net sales—right in line with our 13-15% full-year target. Trade promotion was 55% at $704 million, consumer advertising 45% at $576 million, with digital at 38% of the budget. Blended A&P ROI improved to 3.4x, up from 2.9x YoY, ahead of P&G's 3.1x and industry 2.5-2.8x.  

North America ROI 3.6x, Europe 3.2x, emerging 3.9x—the highest. Key initiatives: AI-powered incrementality testing, unified measurement ecosystem, portfolio reallocation, DTC synergies. Q4 A&P at 14.5% of sales, ROI 3.3-3.5x.  

As we wrap up, new product launches and our innovation pipeline are key growth engines. New products accounted for 18% of Q3 net sales, up from 14% YoY, contributing 250 bps to organic growth. Radiant Renew skincare hit 25% ACV penetration, $45 million run-rate. VitalFuel Bars $32 million, 48% margins. EcoShield pods $28 million, 52% margins.  

Pipeline: $1.2 billion committed, Q4 NeuroSpark drinks $150 million Year 1; Q1 PureBloom deodorants. Consumer-centric speed cut time-to-market to 15 months, 85% pipeline Planet Positive. Expect 400-500 bps organic from new products in FY24.  

Next, Lisa Gomez will provide an update on our supply chain initiatives.  

Lisa Gomez:  
Thank you, Mike. We continue to focus on optimizing our supply chain to improve efficiency and reduce costs. We are implementing new technologies and processes to enhance our responsiveness to changing market conditions. We are also actively working to mitigate the impact of supply chain disruptions. Our Resilient Core program delivered $120 million H1 savings. Inventory at 65 days, blockchain for 40% produce. Sustainability: 72% recyclable packaging, 85% RSPO-certified sourcing, 15% Scope 3 reduction.  

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.  

Operator:  
Thank you. Instructions for submitting questions will be provided. Our first question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan.  

Emily Chen:  
Could you provide more insight into the geographic performance, particularly in emerging markets?  

Jamie Thompson:  
Thanks, Emily. As Sarah outlined, emerging markets drove 12% organic growth to $5.8 billion, or 38% of sales. Asia-Pacific led at 15%, with China's VitalEssence yogurt up 22% and 2.5 share points. India 18% via rural distribution to 1.2 million villages. Latin America 11%, Brazil beverages 14% volumes despite FX. Middle East/Africa 8%, South Africa personal care 12%. Volumes up 9%, pricing 3%. Initiatives like our Emerging Frontier Fund and AI forecasting improved turns 15%, stockouts down 20%. We're shifting capex to 45% emerging, targeting 45% sales mix by 2025 for 10-15% CAGR potential.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley.  

David Lee:  
How are you managing inventory levels given the current economic uncertainty?  

Sarah Chen:  
Good question, David. Inventory days on hand stabilized at 65 days, down from 78 peak in 2022, thanks to our Resilient Core program and machine learning demand sensing, reducing stockouts 25% and forecast accuracy to 92%. Geopolitical spikes in freight are offset by nearshoring to Mexico and Brazil localization. We've got a $200 million buffer for novel ingredients, dual-sourcing, and blockchain with IBM Food Trust covering 40% produce. This supports 2.2% COGS savings H1, positioning us resilient amid uncertainty.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays.  

Rachel Kim:  
Can you discuss the progress on your sustainability goals and any related cost implications?  

Lisa Gomez:  
Absolutely, Rachel. We've hit 72% recyclable/compostable packaging in H1, up from 55%, including 100% rPET for PureSpring in Europe. Net-zero Scope 1/2 by 2040, 100% recyclable by 2028. 85% RSPO-certified cocoa/palm oil, 15% Scope 3 reduction YoY, unlocking $45 million green premiums from Walmart/Tesco. Cost-wise, APAC palm oil saved 20%, regenerative ag cut 5%, buffering inflation. Vitality Edge productivity added 120 bps to margins. Long-term, precision fermentation targets 300 bps uplift by FY26. Costs are more than offset by savings and premiums.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Tom Wilson with Bank of America.  

Tom Wilson:  
What are your expectations for pricing elasticity in the coming quarters?  

Mike Patel:  
Thanks, Tom. Elasticity held at -0.4 in Q3, better than peers' -0.6, supporting +6.8% NDR without volume erosion. North America resilient at -1.8% volumes on +8.2% pricing, AI dynamic pricing boosted e-comm 18%. Europe -4.2% volumes on selective hikes, emerging +6.5% with flat Brazil soda volumes. Q4 NDR +5-6%, tapering with commodity ease, but innovation like zero-sugar Velocity inflects volumes positive. Full-year pricing +6% to organic guide. Brand equity and insights show 68% stretch-buyers prioritizing quality.  

Operator:  
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Jamie Thompson for closing remarks.  

Jamie Thompson:  
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your insightful questions. We remain committed to delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders through our Powering Everyday Essentials strategy. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Vitality Brands Q3 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
